logo_override.validation_detail: HTTP 200, content-type image/png, 9423 bytes, 180x180, 100% opaque (no transparency to bleed onto a card); canvas pixel audit mean luminance 171 with 38% dark pixels, and rendered on a white background it shows the University of Geneva logotype plus keyhole seal in UNIGE red, fully legible
logo_override._award: Excellence Master Fellowships (Faculty of Science, University of Geneva)

notes: The University of Geneva publishes exactly one file-backed wordmark and it is white, so it was rejected and a coloured official mark substituted. Probed: /cdn/themes/unige2016/img/unige-logo.svg is the wordmark every unige.ch page uses in its header - webfetch returned the raw SVG and every path is fill="#FFFFFF"; rendered on white it is completely invisible, so it fails rule 3. /cdn/themes/unige2016/img/unige-logo.png is the same wordmark as a raster (164x47, 47% opaque, mean luminance 255, 100% light pixels) - also white, also rejected. I then grepped the theme stylesheet https://www.unige.ch/cdn/themes/unige2016/css/styles.min.css (200, 1.1 MB) for url(...) logo references and found none, which confirms UNIGE never serves the logo as a CSS background and so there is no hidden dark variant there. Probed and 404: unige-logo-black/-couleur/-color/-rouge/-bleu.svg, logo-unige.svg/.png, logo.svg, and at the site root logo.svg, logo.png, brand.svg, og-image.png, share.png. Accepted /apple-touch-icon.png: HTTP 200, image/png, 9423 B, 180x180, fully opaque, and visually confirmed on white to be the UNIGE logotype and keyhole seal in UNIGE red. /favicon.ico (200, image/vnd.microsoft.icon, 1285 B) is the same seal reduced to 16x16 - too small to use, so the 180x180 PNG was preferred. The existing record image was an official_banner, not a logo. Caveat for the merge: this is the square app-icon composition of the UNIGE mark rather than a full-width horizontal wordmark, because UNIGE does not publish the horizontal dark variant as a file.
